To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a small RAM can be used to improve the performance of a low-cost SSD, and that the key to doing this is a clever mapping data-structure design and host-assisted hint mechanism.

a small amount of host RAM can be used to compensate for the lack of RAM within the disk, and that the resulting SSD performs only 2 + ε physical accesses for every request of page-size blocks by the host, even when the SSD is full and garbage collection is active.
we can achieve high performance with a low-cost SSD, and that we can prototype an SSD without having to build a hardware prototype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, prototyping, and evaluation of high-performance low-cost SSDs.
the following questions: 1) Can a low-cost SSD be built that is as fast as a high-performance SSD, and 2) can it be done with a small amount of on-SSD RAM?
the following problem: How can we design a high-performance SSD that is also low-cost?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we are able to design and implement a working prototype of an innovative SSD that performs only a constant number of physical accesses to the NAND flash for each request of a page-sized block, for all access patterns.
we present a new architecture for SSDs that has the potential to achieve high performance at low cost.
our prototype design for an SSD achieves the performance of a high-performance SSD with a small amount of memory and low cost.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have prototyped a high-performance lowcost solid-state disk that can be built for less than $1 per GB of flash storage.
we have prototyped an SSD with high performance and low cost, and have done it in a way that allows us to easily change the design.
we have designed a high-performance low cost SSD that can be prototyped in software.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a small RAM is sufficient to achieve high performance in an SSD if the host is used to assist the SSD in its garbage collection, and if the SSD is designed with an appropriate data structure.
a high-performance lowcost SSD is achievable with a small RAM, if the SSD uses the right design ideas.
the performance of a low-cost SSD can be improved by using a clever mapping data-structure and host-assisted hint.
